t: Why This Channel Exists (and why I hate Houston)

q.x: For those interested in urban planning, including contrasts between the US and places that do it well, I highly recommend the Not Just Bikes [link] channel. The intro video details a short walk in Houston, which is pretty alarming: [link]

desc:
Watch this video ad-free on Nebula: https://nebula.tv/videos/not-just-bikes-why-city-design-is-important-and-why-i-hate-houston

I'm not an urban planner, so you might ask, why do I run a YouTube channel about urban planning and walkable cities? It all comes down to a life of travel, and a terrible walk in the suburbs of Houston.

Subway lines in a city are more expensive, around $200-400 M / mile, but of course there are fewer miles to cover, so the result is the same. New York pays an excessive $2.5 billion per mile, but my understanding is that is due more to corruption and red tape.

recs.x:
The point you're making is exactly the problem. The reason bus lines aren't used more is because they suck in a lot of cities. Improving the public transportation infrastucture (and no, not taxis), would solve this problem - as demonstrated in many European cities.

Here's a good video that compares the city planning of Houston to other cities, and explains why it sucks. It focuses more on cars vs. bikes, but the same basic point also applies to public transportation: [link]

> Its hard to build roads, highways, sewers these days without some pushback. We need to start changing our views and start seeing constriction as an essential human need and return to the old view of infrastructure as something we take pride in

For me, it's not "construction" by itself, but I suspect it's pushback against urban sprawl and poor urban design. I watched an excellent video about Houston: [link] It takes awhile to get to the point, so you might want to skip to 3:42.
